doc.title: Melba Liston — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Depression years, church and singing
summary: Liston cannot recall the family's finances but says there were no problems; she attended Unity church and sang only occasionally.

story.theme_name: Church, faith and religion in a musician's life
story.community_name: Church, faith and jazz: the sacred and the secular

blocks.x: [asks about the family’s economic situation in Kansas City during the Depression.]
[cannot remember]. But we didn’t have no problems.
Did you sing in church? Is that where you started singing? Because you do sing.
Okay. But when you were little, did you sing in the children’s choir or something?
No. Just sing in church. Okay. With the congregation.
Yeah. And when I’m home, the radio.
Most jazz musicians started in church. That’s why I’m trying to get to that. Watson: What church were you in?
